title: Grade 4 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — General Assessment #20

pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In which months of the usual calendar does Maha Shivratri usually fall? (1 mark)
   A. July or August
   B. February or March
   C. December or January
   D. October or November

2. Which activity is suggested to learn about festivals? (1 mark)
   A. Write a composition on your favourite festival
   B. Copy a friend's essay
   C. Watch television all day
   D. Read a book quietly

3. Which is a benefit of praying every day? (1 mark)
   A. It makes us taller
   B. It makes homework disappear
   C. It stops all rain
   D. It teaches discipline

4. How should you dress to visit a Mandir? (1 mark)
   A. Wearing school uniform
   B. Modestly
   C. Wearing a heavy coat
   D. Very informally

5. Which is the most famous sacred river in Hindu teaching? (1 mark)
   A. Athi
   B. Tana
   C. Nzoia
   D. Ganga

6. What is a good posture for prayer? (1 mark)
   A. Eat snacks
   B. Jump around
   C. Lie down and talk
   D. Sit calmly with hands folded

7. In which Kenyan towns are Mandirs found? (1 mark)
   A. Only in villages
   B. Only Lamu
   C. Nairobi, Mombasa and Kisumu
   D. None

8. In a maize farm, what does the sun's heat that ripens the crop represent among the elements? (1 mark)
   A. Jal
   B. Akash
   C. Agni
   D. Prithvi

9. In the story of the swan, who shot the swan? (1 mark)
   A. Siddhartha
   B. Prahlad
   C. Suddhodana
   D. Devadatta

10. Maha Shivratri means what? (1 mark)
   A. The great day of the Sun
   B. The festival of lights
   C. The great night of Shiva
   D. The day of forgiveness

11. What lesson does the Narsimha story teach? (1 mark)
   A. Bullies always win
   B. Kings never make mistakes
   C. Faith is useless
   D. Pride and cruelty do not last

12. Who became the first Prime Minister of Kenya at that time? (1 mark)
   A. Mwai Kibaki
   B. Daniel arap Moi
   C. Jomo Kenyatta
   D. Tom Mboya

13. Which is a use of the Panchang? (1 mark)
   A. Counting rainfall
   B. Keeping the school timetable
   C. Fixing the dates of festivals
   D. Cooking rice

14. Which two heavenly bodies besides the five planets are counted as grahas? (1 mark)
   A. The stars and clouds
   B. Earth and Pluto
   C. The Sun and Earth
   D. The Sun and the Moon

15. What is the lesson of the Harishchandra story? (1 mark)
   A. Lies are useful
   B. Wealth is everything
   C. Truth is worth more than wealth or comfort
   D. Promises are not important

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Name the four Enlightened Beings studied in this lesson. (2 marks)

17. Name two sacred rivers mentioned in the lesson. (2 marks)

18. State two things people do on Maha Shivratri. (2 marks)

19. Why should we visit a friend's festival respectfully? (3 marks)

20. Explain how children who find it hard to speak can join in prayers at assembly. (4 marks)

21. Explain what Hindus mean by an Avtar. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — February or March
   Phalguna usually falls then.

2. A — Write a composition on your favourite festival
   Writing helps us reflect.

3. D — It teaches discipline
   Doing it regularly teaches discipline.

4. B — Modestly
   Modest dress shows respect.

5. D — Ganga
   The Ganga in India is honoured by many Hindus.

6. D — Sit calmly with hands folded
   Calm sitting is respectful.

7. C — Nairobi, Mombasa and Kisumu
   Mandirs are found in many Kenyan towns.

8. C — Agni
   Heat and light belong to Agni.

9. D — Devadatta
   Devadatta shot an arrow at the swan.

10. C — The great night of Shiva
   Maha means great and ratri means night.

11. D — Pride and cruelty do not last
   Good defeats pride in the story.

12. C — Jomo Kenyatta
   Jomo Kenyatta was the first Prime Minister.

13. C — Fixing the dates of festivals
   It lists festival dates.

14. D — The Sun and the Moon
   The seven days link to Sun, Moon and five planets.

15. C — Truth is worth more than wealth or comfort
   The king chose truth.

SECTION B
----
16. (2 marks)
   Answer: Narsimha, Parshvanath, Buddha (Prince Siddhartha) and Sri Guru Ram Das Ji.
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each name.

17. (2 marks)
   Answer: The Ganga and the Beas (or the Rijubalika).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct river.

18. (2 marks)
   Answer: Fast, stay awake all night, bathe the Shiva Linga, offer bel leaves, chant Om Namah Shivaya (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: We listen, ask polite questions, do not laugh at customs, and build peace among communities.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

20. (4 marks)
   Answer: They can hum, listen, join the actions or be helped by friends, so nobody is left out.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for four sensible points.

21. (2 marks)
   Answer: A form in which God is believed to come to earth to protect goodness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for God coming to earth and 1 mark for protecting goodness.
